QA INDEPENDENT RE-MEASUREMENT at delivered sha ba5e8a3d (qa-bf457df2, 2026-08-27 ~06:37Z). VERDICT: APPROVE. Recorded here because the approval summary is write-only and capped.

METHOD. Shared worktree read-only throughout; every leg in `git archive` materializations under %TEMP%\qa-bf457df2\ (mat at parent 364a83f0, mat3 at ba5e8a3d), each `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` EXIT 0, standalone and unpiped, redirected to files so each exit code is its own leg's.

DoD-1 PASS, re-measured at the parent rather than taken on trust: `git grep -n "script-src" 364a83f0 -- apps/daemon/src` returns exactly ONE hit, http-listener-handshake.test.ts:93. No producer had landed, so this is not a duplicate.

DoD-2 PASS - the red reproduces from tracked objects at the parent, which is the whole justification for the row. `pnpm exec vitest run --root apps/daemon --config package.json src/http/http-listener-handshake.test.ts` in the 364a83f0 materialization: EXIT 1, `5 tests | 5 failed`, `AssertionError: expected 'default-src \'self\'; frame-ancestors...' to be 'default-src \'self\'; script-src \'se...' // Object.is equality`. This is a genuine commit-ahead-of-producer defect: the consumer landed at dc36c8d9 (task-527bab5d) asserting the corrected policy while the producer still emitted the old one, and the shared worktree read green only because the fix sat there uncommitted. Exactly the class of false green that a worktree-only gate cannot see.

DoD-3 PASS. `git show --stat ba5e8a3d` = two paths, 14 insertions / 7 deletions, nothing else in the commit; http-listener.test.ts and http-listener-handshake.test.ts untouched. Producer hunk is CSP-only (the frozen header value plus its doc paragraph); test hunks are the two policy assertions. No unrelated hunk rode along.

DoD-4 PASS. Same recipe at ba5e8a3d: `Test Files 2 passed (2)` / `Tests 58 passed (58)`, EXIT 0 - the 5 + 53 split DoD-4 names. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` EXIT 1 with the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` echo, carrying exactly the two pre-carved foreign errors `src/http/affordance-read-planning.test.ts(124,25)` and `(125,25)` TS2339 planningGoalRef (task-48ee1455), quoted verbatim. The commit touches neither that file nor anything it imports, so attribution is structural, not argued.

DoD-5 PASS on the worker's drill, and I ran a SECOND, harder drill of my own rather than only re-reading theirs - because the security-relevant question on this row is not "does the token exist" but "can the style exception silently widen to script".

MY DRILL, in mat3 only (shared worktree never mutated). Mutation: `script-src 'self'` -> `script-src 'unsafe-inline' 'self'` - a real script-inline widening, expressed in a DIFFERENT TOKEN ORDER from the one the negative assertion spells out. Applied and confirmed at static-asset-host.ts:143. Result, frozen-record arm isolated by `-t "frozen record"`: EXIT 1, `Tests 1 failed | 52 skipped (53)`, failing on `AssertionError: expected 'default-src \'self\'; script-src \'un...' to be 'default-src \'self\'; script-src \'se...' // Object.is equality`. Restore proven in a separate call: backup and restored file both SHA256 `0de7ccd9e089404d81d28b195c6bc84a461b981ae24a272404a04f19d8309609`, nonempty on both sides, and equal to `git show ba5e8a3d:apps/daemon/src/http/static-asset-host.ts | sha256sum`.

WHAT THAT DRILL ESTABLISHES, precisely. The suite DOES fail closed on a script-inline widening - the row is safe to land. But the mechanism that caught it is `expectPolicyHeaders`'s exact-value `.toBe(...)` on the whole header, NOT the new `not.toContain("script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'")` arm, which PASSED against my mutant because it is a literal-substring guard sensitive to token order. The commit message says the frozen-record arm "pins both directions ... so the exception cannot silently widen to script"; measured, that arm alone does not - the exact-value assertion is what holds the line. Not blocking and not a rejection: the protection exists and is real. It is disclosed because it is load-bearing knowledge for the next person: if anyone ever relaxes that `.toBe` to a `toContain` or a partial match, the negative assertion will NOT hold the line by itself, and the CSP could widen to inline script with the suite still green. A negative worth keeping would be shape-based (assert the script-src directive's token SET) rather than one literal ordering.

SECURITY READ OF THE POLICY CHANGE ITSELF. Old value had no script-src or style-src, so both inherited `default-src 'self'` - inline style blocked, inline script blocked. New value names `script-src 'self'` explicitly (no change in effect, same-origin only, no `unsafe-eval`, no `data:`) and relaxes style only. `frame-ancestors`, `base-uri` and `object-src` all stay `'none'`, and `x-frame-options: DENY`, `cross-origin-resource-policy: same-origin`, `referrer-policy: no-referrer`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff` are unchanged and still asserted. The residual risk of `'unsafe-inline'` for style is CSS-based exfiltration via selector-driven `url()` fetches - and that is still refused, because `default-src 'self'` continues to bound img/font/connect to same-origin. An attacker who can inject markup can style, not script, and cannot phone home. The relaxation is justified by a real defect: the built bundle sets React inline style attributes for progress widths and status colors, which the old policy blocked in the browser.
